# Quantum Coherence Reuse

> Optimal initial reference mean energy for sequential production of independent coherent qubits with full joint product return.

## Scientific question and central result

For even N≥2, prepare N coherent qubits from fresh |01> pairs while returning the same initially independent reference. Score half trace distance to the reference tensor the complete ideal |+> output batch. The optimal reference mean energy is Theta(sqrt(N/delta)) uniformly at 0<delta≤1/8. The converse permits arbitrary mixed finite-mean references and deterministic time-translation-covariant operations; the upper repeats one finite exactly conserving pair processor.

## Essential distinctions

- Reference mean energy is measured above its ground in qubit-gap units; each input pair already supplies one excitation.
- Global error includes every output and the returned reference. Marginal output quality does not replace this requirement.
- Mixed, unbounded or sparse reference spectra are allowed in the converse when the first energy moment is finite. No variance bound is needed.
- Arbitrary real spectra use time-translation covariance. The finite integer-ladder construction is its periodic special case.
- The successful upper has no reference reset, postselection or discarded subsystem. The same pair unitary is reused; it may depend on the selected reference size.
- A broader covariant optimization and a restricted sequential implementation have the same resource order; their finite optima are not asserted equal.
- General catalytic preparation, quadratic marginal longevity, information-disturbance and sector-recovery tools are prior work. Do not attribute those principles to this result.
- The finite computations exercise stated matrices and instances. They do not prove every parameter, certify priority, or establish an efficient hardware implementation.
